breakfast.name: Kashk-e Bademjan (Persian Eggplant Dip)
breakfast.description: Persian eggplant dip with caramelized onions and kashk (yogurt whey), served with lavash bread. A beloved Iranian breakfast and mezze dish with charred, smoky eggplant
instructions: Prick eggplants with fork
Roast over open flame or in 400°F oven for 20-25 minutes until skin is charred and flesh is soft
Place roasted eggplants in bowl of cold water for 5 minutes until cool enough to handle
Peel away charred skin and discard, chop eggplant flesh coarsely
Heat oil in large pan and sauté sliced onion until golden (about 5 minutes)
Add minced garlic and turmeric, cook for 1 minute until fragrant
Add chopped eggplant and cook for 5-8 minutes, stirring occasionally
Eggplant should break down into creamy consistency
Season with salt, pepper, and 2 tbsp dried mint
Transfer to serving dish
Drizzle kashk generously over top
Garnish with fried onions and additional dried mint
Serve warm or at room temperature with lavash bread or pita for scooping
breakfast.notes: Kashk is Middle Eastern ingredient made from drained yogurt whey or sour milk. Can substitute with Greek yogurt mixed with lemon juice if kashk unavailable
breakfast.fun_fact: Kashk eggplant is a Persian eggplant dip traditionally served with bread like lavash, barbari, pita, or naan. Dried mint is important addition giving dish its distinctive flavor

lunch.name: Kebab Koobideh (Ground Lamb Kebab)
lunch.description: Most popular kebab in Iran - ground lamb on skewers with warming spices. Street food and restaurant staple
instructions: Soak saffron in hot water
Mix ground meat with onion, herbs, spices and saffron water
Knead mixture for 5 minutes until sticky
Wet hands and mold meat onto flat skewers
Grill over charcoal 5-7 minutes, turning frequently
Serve on rice with grilled tomato and onion
lunch.notes: Proper kneading creates cohesive mixture that doesn't fall off skewers. Charcoal grilling essential for authentic taste
lunch.fun_fact: Kebab Koobideh is most popular kebab in Iran, served as street food and in restaurants everywhere. Iran's most iconic lunch

dinner.name: Tahdig (Crispy Rice with Saffron Chicken)
dinner.description: Persian crispy rice crust with saffron chicken - prized dinner dish
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon saffron, steeped in 100ml warm water
instructions: Marinate chicken in yogurt, minced garlic, cinnamon, turmeric, salt 30 minutes
Heat oil in pot, sauté sliced onion until golden
Add marinated chicken with yogurt, cook 20 minutes
Stir in saffron water (reserve some for rice)
Cook until chicken is tender (10 more minutes)
Meanwhile, cook basmati rice: boil in salted water 6-7 minutes until par-cooked
In another pot, heat 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat
Add 1-2 tablespoons of the reserved saffron water to butter
Add a layer of par-cooked rice
Top with half the cooked chicken and sauce
Add remaining rice
Wrap pot lid in kitchen towel to trap steam
Cover and cook on high 1 minute to create tahdig (crispy bottom)
Reduce heat to low, cook 20 minutes covered
Scatter barberries and pistachios on top
Garnish with sumac
Serve by fluffing rice and breaking off tahdig pieces
dinner.notes: Tahdig (crispy rice) is the most prized part - crispy and golden
dinner.fun_fact: In Persian cuisine, getting the best tahdig is a mark of good cooking
